scenes.headline: Android work phones. 2.58M ISP records. A criminal web host.
scenes.body: Three stories that mattered this week
scenes.say: Android work phones, So-net customers, and a criminal web host. Here is your Week in Security for October thirtieth.

scenes.headline: A rogue Android app could pose as Teams
scenes.body: and collect access tokens for your work account
scenes.say: Story one. A flaw in Microsoft Authenticator for Android let a malicious app pretend to be Microsoft Teams, and collect access tokens for your work account.

scenes.headline: CVSS score, rated Important by Microsoft
scenes.source: Microsoft CVE record · The Hacker News
scenes.say: Microsoft scored it eight point six, rated Important, and shipped the fix in September. Microsoft says it has not been exploited.

scenes.headline: Mail, files and calendars
scenes.body: In Enclave's tests. Microsoft says the user must complete a sign-in step.
scenes.say: In Enclave's tests, those tokens opened mail, files and calendars. Microsoft says an attack needs the user to complete a sign-in step in Authenticator.

scenes.headline: records exposed
scenes.say: Story two. Sony Network Communications says attackers broke into the member database of its internet provider So-net, exposing more than two point five eight million customer records.

scenes.headline: Eight days to go public
scenes.say: The break-in happened on October nineteenth. The company shut the server on the twenty-third, confirmed the leak on the twenty-fourth, and went public on the twenty-seventh.

scenes.headline: 54,401 email passwords exposed
scenes.body: Plus names, phone numbers and dates of birth. The passwords were reset.
scenes.source: Sony Network Communications · Help Net Security
scenes.say: Names, phone numbers and dates of birth were exposed, plus fifty-four thousand four hundred and one email passwords. The company has reset those passwords.

scenes.headline: Bulletproof host Virtualine seized
scenes.body: With police in Germany, the Netherlands and the UK
scenes.say: Story three. On October twenty-seventh, the FBI seized the domain of Virtualine, a so-called bulletproof hosting provider, working with police in Germany, the Netherlands and the UK.

scenes.headline: “Ignored more abuse than your last three therapists”
scenes.say: Prosecutors say it kept a criminal forum online after police complaints, and laundered money. It even boasted that it ignored more abuse than your last three therapists.

scenes.headline: Attackers want what already lets you in.
scenes.body: Tokens, passwords and trusted hosting. MFA helps most on an updated device.
scenes.say: Analyst note: the common thread this week is that attackers want what already lets you in. Tokens, passwords, and hosting that looks trusted. Multi-factor authentication helps most on an updated device.

scenes.headline: Do this today
items: Install apps only from trusted stores
So-net customer? Set a new email password
scenes.say: Do this today. Update Microsoft Authenticator on Android. Install apps only from trusted stores. If you are a So-net customer, set a new email password. And treat any message about the breach as suspicious.
